predecessors.name: British Colonial Empire
predecessors.text: 'the state had sovereignty over only the Zanzibar Archipelago and a 16-kilometre-wide (10 mi) strip along the Kenyan coast'; the British protectorate over Zanzibar 'that had existed since 1890' ended…

successors.name: People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba

ledger.x: 10 December 1963: the British protectorate ends and the Sultan of Zanzibar rules a sovereign state.
12 December 1963: the Sultan's coastal strip becomes part of Kenya.
12 January 1964: the revolution ends the Sultanate.
ledger.cpn: People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba

wars.name: Zanzibar Revolution
wars.outcome: The Sultan was deposed on 12 January 1964 and the country renamed the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba; 'the UK did not intervene in the island's unrest' and the page does not say that any territory changed hands.

certainty.note: Island coastlines; the Kenyan coastal strip was fixed by the agreement of 8 October 1963 and ceded on 12 December 1963.
